questions.question: In a certain code language, 'ROM' is coded as '43', and 'ABK' is coded as '11'. How will 'PNB' be coded in that language?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **Sum of the place value - 3**.

Now,

'ROM' is coded as '43', 

⇒ R(18) + O(15) + M(13) - 3

⇒ 18 + 15 + 13 - 3 = 43.

'ABK' is coded as '11',

⇒ A(1) + B(2) + K(11) - 3

⇒ 1 + 2 + 11 - 3 = 11.

Similarly, for **'PNB'**

**⇒ P(16) + N(14) + B(2) - 3**

**⇒ 16 + 14 + 2 - 3 = 29**.

So, 'PNB' will be coded as '29'.

Hence, the correct answer is **"29"**.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'MK - SP' is coded as '-605', and 'AB - TF' is coded as '-194'. How will 'GM - HK' be coded in that language?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **Value of 1st letter pair - Value of 2nd letter pair = Code**.

Now,

'MK - SP' is coded as '-605', 

⇒ M(13) K(11) - S(19) P(16)

⇒ 1311 - 1916 = - 605

'AB - TF' is coded as '-194',

⇒ A(1) B(2) - T(20) F(6)

⇒ 12 - 206 = - 194.

Similarly, for **'GM - HK'**

**⇒ G(7) M(13) - H(8) K(11)**

**⇒ 713 - 811 = - 98**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3"**.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the sixth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the third number is related to the fourth number.

(**NOTE :** Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

11 : 169 :: 13 : 225 :: ? : 361
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **(1st number + 2)² = 2nd number**.

Now,

For, 11 : 169

⇒ (11 + 2)² 

⇒ 13² = 169.

For, 13 : 225

⇒ (13 + 2)2 

⇒ 152 = 225.

Similarly, for **? : 361**

**⇒ (17 + 2)2 **

**⇒ 192 = 361.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"17"**.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'COVER' is coded as '63', 'BASIS' is coded as '50', and 'WISH' is coded as '59'. How will 'GREECE' be coded in that language?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b1ef5af07dc7cdface0347994bbc6f824cbda2bac27bcab0cb4cf07968dfa00.png] 

The logic followed here is:

Logic: Sum of the Place Value.

Now, 

'COVER' is coded as '63',

⇒ C(3) + O(15) + V(22) + E(5) + R(18)

⇒ 3 + 15 + 22 + 5 + 18 = 63.

'BASIS' is coded as '50',

⇒ B(2) + A(1) + S(19) + I(9) + S(19)

⇒ 2 + 1 + 19 + 9 + 19 = 50.

'WISH' is coded as '59'

⇒ W(23) + I(9) + S(19) + H(8)

⇒ 23 + 9 + 19 + 8 = 59.

Similarly, for 'GREECE'

⇒ G(7) + R(18) + E(5) + E(5) + C(3) + E(5)

⇒ 7 + 18 + 5 + 5 + 3 + 5 = 43.

So, 'GREECE' will be coded as '43'.

Hence, the correct answer is "43".

questions.question:
What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘×’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and also ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged?

40 + 10 − 5 × 4 ÷ 5 = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Given equation: 40 + 10 − 5 × 4 ÷ 5 = ? 

Now, if ‘×’ and ‘–‘ and ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged, then:

⇒ __**40 ÷ 10**__ × 5 - 4 + 5 = ? 

⇒ **__4 __**__**×**____** 5**__ - 4 + 5 = ? 

⇒ **__20__** - 4 __**+**____** 5**__ = ? 

⇒ __25____ - 4__ = 21.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

I. Some cars are bikes.

II. No truck is a car.

**Conclusions:**

I. All trucks are bikes.

II. All bikes are cars.

III. All cars are trucks.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
Statement:

I. Some cars are bikes.

II. No truck is a car.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4addec1cbf014dec79016b8421ab41d99ba9a055440c652a6f2b07e7f4bd078b.png] 

Conclusions:

(i) All trucks are bikes - False (Because No definite relation given between trucks and bikes, so it can be possible only).

(ii) All bikes are cars - False (Some car is bike, but all car is bike is possible not definite).

(iii) All cars are trucks - False (No truck is a car)

Here, None of the conclusions follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

**Statements:**

I. No X is G.

II. All B are X.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some G are B.

II. All X are B.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:

I. No X is G.

II. All B are X.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1dfb35ed5416fa9d28880b819ab8b4116551843b0c35efb6b017b9fcb041953e.png] 

Conclusions:

(i) Some G are B - False (All B are X and No X is G, so No B is G).

Here, None of the conclusions follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".
